reformed_baptist.continuationism:
Reformed Baptists commonly hold to cessationism: the view that the miraculous sign gifts of the apostolic age, such as speaking in tongues and apostolic healings, served to confirm the message of the apostles and ceased when that foundational period ended. Scripture is regarded as complete and sufficient, so God no longer gives new revelation through prophecy.

This does not mean Reformed Baptists think God has stopped acting. They pray for the sick, believe God answers prayer, and can speak of his providential healing and care. The difference lies in whether sign gifts continue as ordinary features of church life. Not every Reformed Baptist holds the cessationist view with the same strength. Some describe themselves as cautious or open, but the historic stance, and the one most often taught, is that these gifts have ceased.
